title: Does anyone else visit the same world every night?
content: For the last 14 years of my life, I have visited the same world every time I have what I have come to call the "house dreams." They started off as these houses, just indoors, when I was 10 or 11, with their own rules of reality (mainly, every room you are surprised by what is on the other side of the next door, and rooms keep going one after another) and I am not supposed to be there or explore. I always wanted to go to the third floor. It was special in some way. The best dreams were always up there because the rooms were so much more beautiful. I have slowly branched out to visiting cathedrals and ballrooms and malls and offices and hospitals (and been experimented on in them). I have met an older couple that told me that heaven and Hell are like an hourglass and the dream world is in the point in the middle. IDK if that is true, but I was fully lucid when they told me. I am not particularly religious and was raised atheist. I'm in my early 20s. I am able to draw maps of the world now, because it has branched out to be a whole city. I know the roads when I drive them nearly every night. These dreams don't happen every night, but they are my favorite. Another weird thing is that I keep encountering what I call "tunnels." They can be either tunnels or caves or space between walls, but it's always full of some kind of dust (fiberglass, sand, dirt, dust) and very warm. Sometimes I hear what is comparable to the music in The Princess and the Frog where they meet the man with friends on the other side and the voodoo music happens (sorry I don't know how else to explain the scene) and feel growing fear in these spaces or a deep voice. I do also love going to the beach or the river shore in this world because I pull these beautiful crystals out of the sand. I have only been physically touched by someone in the dream world 4 times in my life, either when someone tried to stop me from turning a corner, pulling me back, or when I one time encountered a boy who said he couldn't leave and had "lost count after 30 years." I know I have an active imagination and I am willing to answer any and all questions. I swear I could write books and books about this. I make art about my experiences as well. All of the pictures on this sub seem to resonate with the liminal aesthetic of my dreams. Can anyone relate to what I've explained? I swear to whatever higher power I can't make this stuff up. My sleeping brain did, and she's hella weird lmao.
